items.title: Compactly generated based spaces and well-pointed objects
items.statement: Throughout this page a based space is CGWH, products are k-products, and based quotients are kified. It is well-pointed when its basepoint inclusion is an unbased cofibration.
items.strategy: Adopt the published CGWH and HEP definitions. Record every later use of well-pointedness; do not assert it for all based spaces.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Smash product of based spaces
items.statement: For based CGWH spaces X,Y, define X∧Y as the kified quotient of X×ₖY by X∨Y, based at the collapsed wedge.
items.strategy: The quotient universal property identifies maps out of X∧Y with maps out of X×ₖY constant on the wedge. The published product-of-quotients result supplies later quotient maps.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Canonical associativity, symmetry, and unit maps for smash products
items.statement: Coordinate permutation, reassociation, and S⁰-unit maps descend to natural based homeomorphisms (X∧Y)∧Z≅X∧(Y∧Z), X∧Y≅Y∧X, and S⁰∧X≅X, satisfying coherence.
items.strategy: Present both triple smashes as the quotient of X×ₖY×ₖZ by the same fat wedge. Quotient products make the coordinate maps descend; inverse and coherence identities hold before quotienting.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Sequential prespectra, spectra, and adjoint structure maps
items.statement: A sequential prespectrum E is well-pointed based CGWH spaces Eₙ and maps σₙ:S¹∧Eₙ→Eₙ₊₁. Its adjoints are Eₙ→ΩEₙ₊₁. Here spectrum means Ω-prespectrum: every adjoint is a weak equivalence.
items.strategy: Fix suspension as S¹∧− and the printed associator. This is a definition in the strict sequential setting, not a stable model-category assertion.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Suspension and sphere prespectra
items.statement: For well-pointed X, Σ∞X has nth space Sⁿ∧X and canonical structure homeomorphisms. The sphere prespectrum 𝕊=Σ∞S⁰ has 𝕊ₙ=Sⁿ.
items.strategy: Iterate the chosen S¹ smash coordinate and invoke associator coherence. No claim that every suspension prespectrum is an Ω-spectrum is made.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Strict maps and structure-compatible homotopies of sequential prespectra
items.statement: A strict map f:E→F has fₙ₊₁σₙ=τₙ(S¹∧fₙ). A compatible homotopy is a level family whose time-t maps obey this equality for every t.
items.strategy: All equalities use the fixed associators. This defines only the strict level category and compatible homotopies.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Stable homotopy groups of a sequential prespectrum
items.statement: For k∈ℤ and any n₀ with n+k≥1 thereafter, πₖ(E)=colimₙ≥n₀ πₙ₊ₖ(Eₙ), with bonding map suspension followed by (σₙ)∗ using the fixed sphere coordinate.
items.strategy: The terms are groups and eventually abelian. The explicit set-colimit relation carries the eventual operations. Tail independence is proved next, so n₀ is not hidden data.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Stable homotopy colimits are independent of a cofinal tail
items.statement: Deleting finitely many terms from the sequential system defining πₖ(E) induces a canonical group isomorphism on colimits.
items.strategy: In the disjoint-union quotient model every class advances to any later tail, and equality is witnessed at a common stage that can also be advanced into the tail. The resulting maps are inverse homomorphisms.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Strict prespectrum maps act functorially on stable homotopy groups
items.statement: A strict map f:E→F of sequential prespectra induces πₖ(f):πₖ(E)→πₖ(F) for every k∈ℤ, compatible with identities and composition; compatible homotopic strict maps induce the same homomorphism. In this sequential-prespectrum setting, f is a stable weak equivalence exactly when πₖ(f) is an isomorphism for every integer k.
items.strategy: Strictness gives a natural transformation of directed systems. Define the map on representatives; the colimit relation proves well-definedness, and published based-homotopy invariance proves the homotopy clause. Then explicitly define stable weak equivalence for strict maps by the all-integer stable-homotopy-group isomorphism criterion. This is a definition, not a claim of a stable model structure or a converse from levelwise maps; May Chapter 25 §6 uses the analogous criterion for spectra.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Shift and suspension of sequential prespectra
items.statement: The shift has (sh E)ₙ=Eₙ₊₁. The sequential suspension sE has (sE)₀=* and (sE)ₙ₊₁=Eₙ, with inherited structure maps. Canonically πₖ(sh E)≅πₖ₋₁(E) and πₖ(sE)≅πₖ₊₁(E).
items.strategy: Both formulas are literal reindexings after deleting finitely many initial terms. This avoids the false claim that levelwise suspension induces an isomorphism for an arbitrary prespectrum.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Stable stems of the sphere
items.statement: The kth stable stem is πₖˢ=πₖ(𝕊)=colimₙ πₙ₊ₖ(Sⁿ), starting where n+k≥1.
items.strategy: This is notation for the preceding colimit with the sphere-prespectrum bonding maps.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Freudenthal identifies the eventual suspension system for spheres
items.statement: For k≥0, πₙ₊ₖ(Sⁿ)→πₙ₊ₖ₊₁(Sⁿ⁺¹) is an isomorphism when n>k+1 and a surjection when n=k+1.
items.strategy: Apply Freudenthal to (n−1)-connected Sⁿ with i=n+k. The isomorphism inequality i<2n−1 is n>k+1; check its suspension map equals the sphere-spectrum bond.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: The sphere prespectrum groups are the classical stable stems
items.statement: For k≥0, πₖ(𝕊) is canonically the eventual value of πₙ₊ₖ(Sⁿ), the classical kth stable homotopy group of spheres.
items.strategy: Every sufficiently late bond is an isomorphism. Map an eventual-stage group into the colimit and invert by advancing any representative to that stage; tail independence makes this canonical.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Pairings and unital multiplication of sequential prespectra
items.statement: A pairing E∧F→G is maps μₘ,ₙ:Eₘ∧Fₙ→Gₘ₊ₙ compatible with both structures, the second using the suspension-coordinate twist. A multiplication has unit S⁰→E₀ and coherent associativity/unit homotopies; commutativity also uses the smash twist and degree-mn sphere permutation.
items.strategy: The article must print both compatibility squares and every associator/twist. The degree-mn permutation is retained rather than replaced by an unexplained sign.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: A ring prespectrum gives a graded product on stable homotopy groups
items.statement: Representatives Sᵐ⁺ᵖ→Eₘ and Sⁿ⁺q→Eₙ smash and compose with μₘ,ₙ to define πₚ(E)×πq(E)→πₚ₊q(E). It is well defined, associative, and unital; commutative data give xy=(−1)^{pq}yx.
items.strategy: Compatibility with each structure map proves independence under stage advance. Homotopy invariance descends associativity and units. For commutativity, compare source block permutation and target degree-mn permutation; the level terms cancel, leaving the Koszul sign pq.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Scope boundary for stable homotopy theory
items.statement: No positive stable stem, Brown representability, stable model structure, replacement, or stable homotopy category is proved. Stable weak equivalence means only the defined all-integer stable-group isomorphism condition on a strict map; consumers may use the sequential definitions, colimit groups, shift bookkeeping, and explicit pairings, but no unproved replacement or localization theorem.
items.strategy: Use the preceding stable weak-equivalence definition to distinguish an all-stable-group isomorphism from strict level homotopy; record the deliberate deferrals without asserting a model category or stable homotopy category.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

title: Spectra and Stable Homotopy Groups: Examples

items.title: The zero stable stem is the integers
items.statement: Degree identifies π₀ˢ with ℤ, with the identity representing 1.
items.strategy: Degree gives πₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ and suspension preserves the oriented generator, so the stable tail is the identity system on ℤ.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Stabilizing a map between spheres
items.statement: A based f:Sⁿ⁺ᵏ→Sⁿ determines a stable class represented by every iterated suspension.
items.strategy: The colimit relation identifies a representative with its suspension; homotopic maps stabilize identically. No unstable recovery is claimed.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Suspension prespectra of spheres are shifts
items.statement: For r≥0, Σ∞Sʳ is canonically the r-fold shift shʳ𝕊, hence πₖ(Σ∞Sʳ)≅πₖ₋rˢ.
items.strategy: At level n both are Sⁿ⁺ʳ; associator coherence identifies structures. Apply the shift formula r times.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: An unstable homotopy class need not yet be stable
items.statement: For X=S¹∨S¹, the nontrivial commutator of its two fundamental-group generators maps to zero under the suspension homomorphism π₁(X)→π₂(ΣX), hence also in the stable homotopy group of the suspension prespectrum of X. This is an explicit failure of injectivity before the Freudenthal stable range.
items.strategy: The published two-circle wedge computation gives π₁(X)=F(a,b), and the reduced-word normal-form theorem proves that aba⁻¹b⁻¹ is nonempty and hence nontrivial. X is connected, so Freudenthal at n=i=1 supplies the suspension homomorphism E:π₁(X)→π₂(ΣX); it promises surjectivity at this endpoint, not injectivity. Collapse the basepoint track in the two-cone suspension; it is a contractible CW subcomplex, so the published collapse lemma identifies Freudenthal’s suspension with the reduced suspension used by the prespectrum on homotopy groups. The target π₂ is abelian by the published higher-homotopy group theorem. Every homomorphism from F(a,b) to an abelian group kills [a,b], so E([a,b])=0. In the suspension prespectrum Σ∞X the stable group is the direct limit of these suspension maps; the same nontrivial stage-one class therefore maps to zero in the colimit. This replaces the undersupplied 2η sphere calculation with a complete elementary witness; it does not assert a value for π₄(S³).

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapters 22 §2 and 25 §§3, 6–7
Hatcher, Spectral Sequences in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2 §2.1

title: Obstruction Theory Postnikov Towers and Classifying Spaces

items.title: Extending over one cell is equivalent to nullhomotoping its attaching sphere
items.statement: For an (n+1)-cell attached to A along α, f:A→Y extends over it iff fα is nullhomotopic.
items.strategy: Restriction proves one direction. Conversely view the disk as the cone on its boundary, descend the nullhomotopy, and glue by the CW pushout universal property.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Homotopy-group local system along a cellular map
items.statement: Let n>=2, let X be a CW complex, and let f:X^n→Y. Since X^n→X induces an isomorphism on fundamental groupoids in the dimensions used here, moving-basepoint transport defines an abelian local system f*Π_n(Y) on X with stalk π_n(Y,f(x)). For n=1 this construction is used only when π_1(Y) is abelian with trivial conjugation action, so the coefficient system is constant; no nonabelian group is placed in an abelian cellular cochain group.
items.strategy: Endpoint-fixed homotopy and path concatenation give the covariant groupoid laws under first-path-first conventions. For n>=2, cells of dimension at least 3 do not change π1, so the f-induced monodromy on X^n extends uniquely to X; for n=1, only the explicit abelian/trivial-action constant system is allowed. This is the pullback of the AT-23 local-system object.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Primary cellular obstruction cochain
items.statement: Let n>=1, (X,A) be a CW pair, and f:X^n∪A→Y. Assume n>=2 with the abelian moving-basepoint local system f*Π_n(Y), or n=1 with π_1(Y) abelian and its conjugation action trivial. Each oriented (n+1)-cell determines the transported class of f on its attaching sphere; these values define θ(f) in C^{n+1}(X,A;f*Π_nY).
items.strategy: The n>=2 or abelian n=1 contract ensures the coefficient group is abelian and is defined over all of X. Characteristic maps and orientations are part of the CW data. Explicit paths type every stalk transport; orientation/lift changes alter basis and coefficient coordinate together.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: The primary obstruction cochain is a cocycle
items.statement: The cochain θ(f) is a cocycle and defines [θ(f)] in local-coefficient cohomology.
items.strategy: For n≥2, use the compatible relative-Hurewicz cell bases on simply connected universal-cover skeleta, the relative homotopy exact sequence, and AT-23 local incidence to show δθ=0. For n=1, put B=X¹∪A and W=X²∪A. Trivial conjugation makes the abelian π₁(Y) coefficients constant in supplied component coordinates; first Hurewicz factors f_* through λ:H₁(B;Z)→π₁(Y). The value on each relative two-cell e is λ(∂[D²_e,S¹_e]). For an attaching three-cell, its cellular two-boundary is the image in H₂(W,B;Z) of its attaching-sphere class in H₂(W;Z), so the pair homology long exact sequence gives λ∂i_*=0. This retains arbitrary A and requires no global choice. AT-23 cellular-cochain comparison yields the singular local-coefficient class.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Difference cochain between two cellular extensions
items.statement: Under the same abelian coefficient-system hypotheses as the primary obstruction cochain, let f_0,f_1:X^n∪A→Y and a homotopy on X^{n−1}∪A be given. The obstruction on each prism e^n×I, with interval-last orientation and coefficient identification along that homotopy, defines d(f_0,f_1) in C^n(X,A;f_0*Π_nY).
items.strategy: Use (X×I)ⁿ=(Xⁿ×∂I)∪(Xⁿ⁻¹×I), interval-last orientations, and transport along the supplied homotopy. This definition precedes every prism identity.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: The primary obstruction class is independent of cellular choices
items.statement: Changing cellular representatives, transport coordinates, or the nth-skeleton extension with fixed prior stage changes θ by a coboundary under the canonical coefficient identification.
items.strategy: AT-23 handles basis/transport changes. On e×I, ∂(e×I)=(∂e)×I+(−1)ⁿ(e×1−e×0), so the cocycle equation gives θ(f₁)−θ(f₀)=±δd.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Vanishing of the primary obstruction is equivalent to extension over the next skeleton
items.statement: Assuming AC for an arbitrary cell family, f|Xⁿ⁻¹∪A extends over Xⁿ⁺¹∪A iff [θ(f)]=0. Finite relative CW pairs need only finite choice.
items.strategy: Follow Davis–Kirk §7.4, Lemma 7.8 and Proposition 7.10 with AT-23 transports. Necessity: an actual extension makes every attaching-sphere class zero. Sufficiency: if [θ]=0, choose d with θ=δd. On each n-cell prism D^n×I, the lower disk and side cylinder are already prescribed; their union is contractible. The homotopy extension property on the boundary sphere lets one realize the desired d(e^n) while fixing that prescribed part (Davis–Kirk Lemma 7.11). For an arbitrary set of n-cells, AC selects these prism extensions; this is the declared AC use. The CW pushout glues their top faces to a modified map f′ on X^n, stationary on X^{n−1}∪A. The interval-last prism boundary identity gives θ(f)−θ(f′)=δd, hence θ(f′)=0. The one-cell nullhomotopy criterion and CW gluing extend f′ over every (n+1)-cell; selecting all arbitrary cell fillers also uses AC. For a finite relative CW pair, only finitely many choices are made.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Difference cochains classify homotopies in the stable stage
items.statement: Assume AC. When lower homotopy groups vanish and the π₁-action is simple, the difference class vanishes exactly when two extensions are homotopic rel A through the next skeleton; nonempty extension classes form the indicated cohomology torsor.
items.strategy: Apply the extension theorem to (X×I,X×∂I∪A×I). The prism boundary shifts cellular cochains and identifies its obstruction with the difference class. Cocycle modifications give a free transitive action. The AC hypothesis is inherited from the arbitrary-cell realization/extension step of the cited obstruction or representability theorem.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Obstruction theory for lifting through a fibration
items.statement: Assume AC and n>=1. For a Serre fibration with path-connected simple fiber F, the obstruction to extending a lift from Xⁿ∪A lies in Hⁿ⁺¹(X,A;f*ΠₙF), and class-zero is equivalent to extension after altering the nth-stage lift. Numerable bundles enter through the published fibration theorem.
items.strategy: Pull back over X. Trivialize over each disk by lifting its contraction, read the boundary section in πₙ(F), and assemble with fiber transport. The cellular cocycle and difference arguments apply. Arbitrary simultaneous lift choices inherit the AC declaration from the extension theorem. Construct the varying-fiber pi_n local system by finite relative Serre lifting and simple-fiber basepoint correction.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces
items.statement: K(G,1) has π₁≅G and no higher homotopy; for abelian A and n≥2, K(A,n) has πₙ≅A and all other positive groups zero. Models are connected CW complexes with chosen identifications.
items.strategy: The abelian restriction in degree n≥2 follows from higher homotopy abelianness. No nonabelian K(G,n), n≥2, is asserted.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Existence and homotopy uniqueness of Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces
items.statement: Assuming AC, K(G,1) exists for every group and K(A,n) for every abelian A,n≥2; CW models with the same identified group are homotopy equivalent compatibly with that identification.
items.strategy: Use Davis–Kirk §7.7 Theorem 7.20 and Hatcher §4.3. For n=1 take a presentation of G, make a wedge of one circle per generator, attach 2-cells along all relators, then for k>=2 attach (k+1)-cells along representatives of a generating set for π_k to kill it without changing lower groups; cellular approximation and van Kampen prove π1=G throughout. For n>=2 start with a wedge of n-spheres indexed by generators of A, attach (n+1)-cells for the abelian relations so π_n=A by relative Hurewicz, and kill higher π_k successively in the same way. AC is used to choose generating sets, representatives and arbitrary attaching maps; at the end the weak CW union has the prescribed homotopy groups because each compact sphere map meets a finite subcomplex. For uniqueness, construct a map inducing the chosen group isomorphism: for n=1 map 1-cells according to the group homomorphism, fill relator 2-cells, then extend because all higher target groups vanish; for n>=2 use the corresponding n-sphere map and the obstruction/coefficient argument. The induced map is a weak equivalence and published Whitehead promotes it to homotopy equivalence. Handle basepoints and the nonabelian n=1 case separately; do not apply an abelian n>=2 obstruction cochain to nonabelian π1.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces represent singular cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC. For based CW X, abelian A, and n≥1, a fundamental class ι induces [X,K(A,n)]*≅H̃ⁿ(X;A), naturally; for connected X and n>0 this is ordinary Hⁿ.
items.strategy: Use Davis–Kirk §7.7, Theorem 7.22, and the published AT-23 cellular–singular cochain comparison. Define the fundamental class ι∈H^n(K(A,n);A) as the UCT/Hurewicz class corresponding to id_A, with n=1 using abelian π1. Given a cocycle c∈C^n(X;A), map X^n/X^{n−1}=∨S^n to K(A,n) with degree/class c(e^n) on each cell; δc=0 says every (n+1)-cell attaching map becomes nullhomotopic, so the map extends across X^{n+1}. All higher obstructions vanish since π_iK(A,n)=0 for i>n; AC handles arbitrary simultaneous cell choices. This proves surjectivity of the cellular obstruction map Ψ. For maps f,g with the same obstruction class, the prism/difference-cochain formula gives d(f,g)=Ψ(f)−Ψ(g)=0, so their homotopy extends across the n-cells; all higher homotopy obstructions vanish, proving injectivity. On the identity of K(A,n), evaluate the difference cocycle on an n-cell relative Hurewicz generator to show Ψ(id)=ι; naturality then gives Ψ(f)=f*ι. Finally use AT-23 to identify cellular and singular H^n, and adjust based/reduced conventions: for connected X,n>0 the reduced and ordinary groups agree. Do not cite representability as a premise.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Cohomology operations are universal classes on Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. For abelian A and B, n≥1 and integer r, natural operations on reduced cohomology of based CW complexes H̃ⁿ(−;A)→H̃ⁿ⁺ʳ(−;B) correspond to universal classes in H̃ⁿ⁺ʳ(K(A,n);B) by pullback; no additivity is assumed. For a family indexed by n≥1, commutation with suspension in positive source degrees is equivalent to compatibility of its universal classes with cohomology suspension. Full stability indexed by all integers also requires the degree-zero suspension identity. For connected CW complexes with positive source and target degrees this gives the ordinary-cohomology formulation; the target-degree-zero case stays reduced.
items.strategy: Write x=f*ι. Naturality forces θ(x)=f*θ(ι); conversely pull back a universal class. Use the earlier singular prism chain homotopy, dualized to relative cochains with arbitrary coefficients B, to prove independence of the based classifying map. In positive source degrees, the suspension square is equivalent to compatibility of universal classes; this does not settle the degree-zero identity in the full stable-operation definition. AC is inherited from the representability supplier.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Postnikov sections and Postnikov towers
items.statement: An nth Postnikov section X→PₙX preserves πᵢ for i≤n and has πᵢ(PₙX)=0 for i>n. A tower has compatible maps PₙX→Pₙ₋₁X in the homotopy category.
items.strategy: Record basepoints and π₁-actions. Compatibility is up to specified homotopy unless a strict model is chosen; no inverse-limit recovery is asserted.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Postnikov towers exist for connected CW complexes
items.statement: Assuming AC, every connected CW complex admits Postnikov sections and compatible tower maps, by attaching cells of dimension at least n+2 to kill homotopy above n without changing lower groups.
items.strategy: At each r>n attach (r+1)-cells along chosen generators of πᵣ. The relative LES kills πᵣ and preserves lower groups. AC supplies all representatives. Compactness of spheres and disks identifies homotopy of the increasing CW union with the colimit; the universal property gives tower maps up to homotopy.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Postnikov k-invariants
items.statement: Assume AC. For a connected based space (X,x₀) and n≥2, a marked Postnikov stage PₙX→Pₙ₋₁X with fiber K(πₙ(X,x₀),n) has kₙ₊₁(X) in Hⁿ⁺¹(Pₙ₋₁X;𝒜), where 𝒜 records the π₁(X,x₀)-action. For simple X this is ordinary cohomology with constant coefficient πₙ(X,x₀) and is represented by a based map to K(πₙ(X,x₀),n+1); no untwisted map is asserted for nontrivial action.
items.strategy: Fix the basepoint and fiber identification. The primary section obstruction defines the local-coefficient class for general connected X, and a fiber-homotopy equivalence with fixed base and fiber markings transports it. Only when X is simple does the local system become constant and representability give a based map to K(πₙ(X,x₀),n+1). The AC hypothesis is inherited from the arbitrary-cell realization/extension step of the cited obstruction or representability theorem.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Simple Postnikov stages are classified by k-invariants
items.statement: Assume AC. For n>=2, connected simple CW (n-1)-type B and abelian A, marked ordinary Hurewicz fibration stages over B with fiber of CW homotopy type K(A,n), trivial monodromy and marked π_n≅A are classified up to marked fiber homotopy equivalence by k∈H^{n+1}(B;A). The representative is the terminal-path homotopy fiber of κ:B→K(A,n+1); unmarked stages over the fixed base correspond to Aut(A)-orbits.
items.strategy: Use the low-degree cohomological Serre transgression to identify the primary section obstruction and exact segment H^n(E;A)→End(A)→H^{n+1}(B;A)→H^{n+1}(E;A). A nullhomotopy of κq gives a preliminary map to the path pullback; correct its fiber endomorphism by a global H^n(E;A) class, then use May–Ponto fiber-homotopy promotion. Path reversal fixes the terminal-path sign, and Schön supplies CW type for Hurewicz total and loop fibers.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21
May and Ponto, More Concise Algebraic Topology, §3.4 Lemma 3.4.2, pp.57–61
Schön, Fibrations Over a CWh-Base, Theorem 2 and Proposition 3, p.165

items.title: Universal principal bundles and classifying spaces
items.statement: For a well-pointed topological group G of CW type, a universal numerable principal bundle is EG→BG with EG contractible. Classification below is for numerable bundles; paracompact bases require a separate numerability theorem.
items.strategy: Fix right actions and a based orbit. Contractibility alone is not treated as universality; the Milnor model and pullback construction supply it.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Milnor’s infinite-join model of EG
items.statement: For a topological group G, EG=G*G*⋯ consists of finite formal sums ∑tᵢgᵢ with tᵢ≥0 and sum 1, modulo zero-weight labels. For compact Hausdorff G it carries the ordinary weak direct-limit topology of compact finite quotient joins; otherwise it carries the ordinary un-kified coordinate-label strong topology. G acts diagonally and BG=EG/G has the ordinary orbit quotient topology.
items.strategy: Retain finite quotient joins as set models. Select their ordinary weak compact-stage colimit for compact Hausdorff G, giving the literal finite-projective weak CW unions for S¹ and Z/2; otherwise select Milnor's ordinary coordinate-label strong topology. Neither branch is additionally kified. The theorem proves ordinary action, charts, contraction, and support-subordinate numeration in each branch.

references.title: Milnor, Construction of Universal Bundles II, §§2–3
tom Dieck, Algebraic Topology, §14.4.3

items.title: Finite join models for the circle and the two-point group
items.statement: For every N≥0, the join of N+1 circles is equivariantly homeomorphic to S^{2N+1}, and the join of N+1 two-point groups is equivariantly homeomorphic to S^N; the orbit spaces are CP^N and RP^N respectively, compatibly with the finite-stage inclusions.
items.strategy: Use the explicit coordinate maps (t_i,z_i)↦(sqrt(t_i)z_i) and (t_i,epsilon_i)↦(epsilon_i sqrt(t_i)). Recover weights and positive-weight labels to prove bijectivity, then use compact-to-Hausdorff to obtain homeomorphisms and check equivariance directly.

references.title: Dale Husemoller, Fibre Bundles, Third Edition, Chapter 4, Examples 11.3–11.4

items.title: Milnor’s join model is a contractible free G-space
items.statement: The selected ordinary-topology EG has free diagonal G-action, is contractible, and EG→BG is a support-subordinate numerable principal G-bundle with ordinary charts. For G=S¹ or Z/2, its base is literally the standard weak CW colimit CP∞ or RP∞.
items.strategy: A positive coordinate proves freeness. In the noncompact strong branch, fixed-output weights and positive labels establish ordinary continuity of the tail-splitting contraction, cone, action, parity homotopies, and disjoint interpolation. In the compact weak branch, finite quotient joins are compact Hausdorff with closed inclusions; the finite-product k-omega theorem reduces ordinary product continuity to compact-stage quotient formulas, proving those same maps without a false compact-image factorization. Normalize positive labels for inverse ordinary principal charts. Refine coordinates by wᵢ=max(0,tᵢ−∑_(j<i)t_j) and threshold normalized weights so their closed supports lie in Uᵢ. Orbit quotients preserve the compact-stage final topology, giving literal weak CW CP∞ and RP∞ for S¹ and Z/2.

references.title: Milnor, Construction of Universal Bundles II, §§2–3 and 5
tom Dieck, Algebraic Topology, §§14.4.1–14.4.6 and 14.4.12
Husemoller, Fibre Bundles, Chapter 4, §§11–12

items.title: Numerable principal bundles are classified by maps to BG
items.statement: Assuming AC, pullback gives [X,BG] bijective with isomorphism classes of numerable principal G-bundles over a CGWH base X. Paracompactness is usable only with a separate theorem producing numerability.
items.strategy: A numeration and local sections define an equivariant P→EG by finite weighted coordinates, hence X→BG; local finiteness gives continuity. Pullback recovers P. Pullback over X×I proves homotopy invariance. AC handles arbitrary indexed local data.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: The based loop space of BG recovers G weakly
items.statement: Assume AC. For well-pointed G of CW type, path lifting gives an endpoint-label map ε:ΩBG→G; with the library convention the fibration boundary is ∂(γ)=ε(γ)⁻¹. Both are weak equivalences. If both spaces have CW type, Whitehead upgrades them to based homotopy equivalences.
items.strategy: Use AC through the numerable-bundle lifting-function theorem. The fibration LES and contractibility of EG make ∂:ΩBG→G an isomorphism on every homotopy group and a component bijection. Inversion is a homeomorphism, so ε is weak as well; invoke Whitehead only with its printed hypotheses.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: The classifying space of a discrete group is a K(G,1)
items.statement: Assume AC. For discrete G, Milnor BG is connected with π₁≅G and πₙ=0 for n>1; a CW model is K(G,1).
items.strategy: The loop weak equivalence gives πₙ(BG)≅πₙ₋₁(G). A discrete group has components G and no positive homotopy. The join model is connected; CW replacement preserves these groups.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

title: Obstruction Theory Postnikov Towers and Classifying Spaces — Examples

items.title: Primary obstruction to a nowhere-zero section of a sphere fibration
items.statement: Assume AC. For r>=1 and a numerable S^r-fibration, the first possible section obstruction lies in H^{r+1}(X,A;𝒫), with stalk π_r(S^r)≅Z and orientation monodromy.
items.strategy: For r>=1 the sphere is (r−1)-connected; r=0 is excluded because π0(S0) is a pointed set, not the asserted integer local system. Apply lifting obstruction in degree r and degree classification for the stalk; fiber transport gives the sign local system. No Euler-class identification is asserted. The AC hypothesis is inherited from the arbitrary-cell realization/extension step of the cited obstruction or representability theorem.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Infinite complex projective space is K(Z,2)
items.statement: Assume AC. Despite its legacy ID, this states CP∞≃K(ℤ,2), not K(ℤ,1). The universal circle bundle has contractible total space.
items.strategy: Apply the fibration LES to S¹→S∞→CP∞, using π₁(S¹)=ℤ and vanishing higher groups. Preserve the stable ID and record the mismatch.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Real projective infinity as BZ/2
items.statement: Assume AC. The antipodal universal double cover identifies RP∞ with B(ℤ/2)=K(ℤ/2,1).
items.strategy: S∞ is contractible and the antipodal action is free; identify its quotient and apply the discrete-group corollary.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: First nontrivial Postnikov stage of a simply connected space
items.statement: If X is simply connected and n≥2 is least with πₙX≠0, then PₙX is K(πₙX,n).
items.strategy: The section preserves groups through n and kills those above; minimality kills those below. Higher homotopy abelianness supplies the valid coefficient group.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: The trivial principal bundle has a nullhomotopic classifying map
items.statement: The trivial numerable bundle corresponds to the constant map; a nullhomotopic classifying map pulls back a trivial bundle.
items.strategy: A global section makes the coordinate construction constant. Pullback along a constant map is X×G, and homotopy invariance handles any nullhomotopic map.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Incompatible choices do not define one global obstruction problem
items.statement: There is a CW pair (X,A), a fixed map A→S¹, and two 2-cells such that each cell separately admits an extension after a suitable choice of the map on the common 1-cell, but no single choice extends across both cells. For a fixed map on the entire 1-skeleton, zero obstruction on every cell does give a global extension by CW gluing.
items.strategy: Take X with one vertex, 1-cells a,b, and two 2-cells attached along the based words ab and ab². Let A be the b-circle and fix f:A→S¹ of degree 1. A map on the remaining 1-cell a has an arbitrary integer degree k, represented by a standard circle loop. The attaching maps of the two 2-cells then have image degrees k+1 and k+2 by the published concatenation/power degree laws. The first cell alone extends for k=−1 and the second alone for k=−2, since a based circle loop extends over a disk exactly when its degree is zero. A simultaneous extension would require k+1=k+2=0, impossible. The independently vanishing obstructions use different maps on the same 1-skeleton; this is the exact quantifier distinction. For one fixed 1-skeleton map, if every cell obstruction vanishes, choose disk fillings and glue them along the attaching maps by the CW pushout (AC only if the cell family is infinite; this example has two). The original claimed fixed-map counterexample is false and is explicitly rejected.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21

items.title: Principal-bundle classification can fail without numerability
items.statement: Milnor’s universal principal GL₁(R)-bundle classifies numerable bundles, but the frame bundle of the tangent line bundle of a smooth long line is a locally trivial principal GL₁(R)-bundle that is not numerable and therefore is not a pullback of Milnor’s bundle. The long line here is allowed to lack the library’s second-countability manifold convention.
items.strategy: Use Nyikos, The Topological Structure of the Tangent and Cotangent Bundles on the Long Line, Topology Proceedings 4 (1979), pp271–276, for the classical smooth connected Hausdorff long line L, its tangent line bundle, and its nonmetrizability. Its frame bundle P=F(TL) is locally trivial with structure group GL₁(R) by chart differentials. Suppose P had a numerable trivializing cover (U_i) with locally finite partition of unity (φ_i) subordinate to it. Each trivialization gives a continuous positive quadratic norm g_i on TL|U_i; g=Σ_i φ_i g_i is a globally continuous positive-definite quadratic form because the sum is locally finite and Σφ_i=1. For a connected 1-manifold with such g, define d_g(p,q) as the infimum of lengths of piecewise C¹ paths. Fixed p,q lie in a compact bounded order interval of L, covered by finitely many charts, so d_g(p,q)<∞. In a smaller coordinate interval around p, g has positive upper and lower bounds; local line segments show d_g-balls contain ordinary neighborhoods, while any path leaving a compact inner interval pays a fixed positive length, so small d_g-balls lie in the chart and d_g induces the original topology. Thus L would be metrizable, contradicting Nyikos. Every pullback of Milnor EG→BG is numerable by pulling back its join-coordinate partition; hence P cannot be such a pullback. This is a topological principal-bundle example over a non-second-countable base, outside the paracompact/CW classification claim.

references.title: Davis–Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 7 and §8.6
Miller, MIT 18.906 Algebraic Topology II, Lectures 12–15 and 17–21
Peter J. Nyikos, The Topological Structure of the Tangent and Cotangent Bundles on the Long Line, Topology Proceedings 4 (1979), 271–276
